cells.tense: You are sitting inside something that lasted because it was worth handing down.
cells.act: write the order things go in
cells.ask: Take one practice your group keeps — a meal, a reading, a way you mark a season — and write down the order it moves in, so it still runs the same on the night you can't be there to walk anyone through it.
cells.core:
Inside a tradition you're part of, you can tell which pieces matter without being able to explain it. You know which part to protect and which to let settle, and people notice it when you're around — the thing makes more sense with you nearby. That isn't analysis. It's a read that lands before the reasoning does, and when it speaks you tend to go along with it.

The balance is worth keeping, and there's a step that keeps it. Take one arrangement that already works — how the group gathers, what order the parts go in — and set it down somewhere it can outlast your presence. Written, or handed to whoever will carry it. Then it stops needing you to hold it up.
cells.sheetLine: What you know here is worth setting down where it outlasts you.
cells.place: In the shared meaning and traditions people pass along

cells.tense: You will keep gathering what the tradition holds, and it will not make you sure.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Out of everything you've been collecting about the tradition you belong to, choose the piece you'd mind losing most, and turn toward that piece first. Leave the rest in the drawer.
cells.core:
Around the tradition you belong to, you've gone to the record — reading, comparing, asking, gathering. This kind of knowing was not going to arrive through more material. It comes from seeing what counts before you have reasons. The collecting has been standing in for that, and by now it's a wall: the more you take in, the less anything gets through, because each arrival has to be checked against what you already filed.

You're allowed to want the thing itself, not proof about it. Choose the belief or practice you'd mind losing most, and turn to face that one. Not to defend it, not to settle it — just to stand in front of it. That pull is a compass, and it's been under the notes the whole time.
cells.sheetLine: You've read enough. Turn toward the one you'd miss.
cells.place: In the shared meaning and traditions people pass along

cells.tense: You had a read you trusted, and it stopped being yours to trust.
cells.act: sketch the whole of it badly, on one page, and keep the sketch
cells.ask: On a single page, sketch how the tradition you're part of holds together for you — messily, no tidy order — and keep the page. Not to get it right. To see what your hand reaches for first.
cells.core:
In the traditions you're part of, you stopped trusting what you saw. A practice meant something once, and the meaning doesn't come the way it used to, so you've been asking other people what's true about it — checking your read against the room before you'll hold it. It used to arrive without the checking. Now there's fog where it was, and asking has become the way you keep your footing.

Fog isn't the absence of a path. You walk it by taking one step with only enough light for that step. Sketch how the whole thing holds together for you, badly, on a page — let your hand choose what goes where instead of deciding. Keep the sketch. A week later, read it and see what you reached for before you reasoned.
cells.sheetLine: The knowledge didn't leave. It stopped being trusted.
cells.place: In the shared meaning and traditions people pass along

cells.tense: Reads about what to keep arrive, and by the time you notice them they have already been acted on.
cells.act: give back what is owed, and take what is yours
cells.ask: Pick an obligation you've been carrying inside a shared custom — a role, a duty, a way of doing it. Notice who it serves now, name that to yourself once, honestly, then hand it back or take it as yours.
cells.core:
Around the customs you share, things keep turning out a certain way and you'd call it chance. The group drops a practice, keeps another, and later the kept one proves to have been the right call — but you didn't decide, or don't remember deciding. Something in you got there first, and got there accurately. What's missing is that you were the one who got there.

Attribution is the whole act here. Take one duty you carry inside a custom — a role, a way of doing it that has become yours — and say plainly to yourself who it holds up. If it's holding others, hand it back. If it's yours, take it as yours. Not a reckoning. A name put on something already true.
cells.sheetLine: The read is accurate. That it's yours hasn't caught up yet.
cells.place: In the shared meaning and traditions people pass along

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person's knowing in this seat has been disowned — that perceptions arrived and got filed as chance. Many people transmit a tradition competently without any buried authorship, and a reader could reasonably say this is just the ordinary seam between what one generation holds and the next. The ask survives that: naming who one carried practice actually serves is useful whether or not anything was buried, and it teaches the person something about their own grip on the thing. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the one about the group being held up by a hand no one has named — the record doesn't say others depend on them, so I've cut it to the naming and nothing downstream of it.
